title: hour
summary: Extract hour components from datetime values in MATLAB and RunMat.

gpu_support.notes: Documented datetime and legacy serial/text inputs execute on the host. RunMat-only resident inputs gather through their owning provider after compatibility admission.

description: `hour(t)` extracts hour-of-day values from datetime input. The documented legacy forms also accept serial date numbers or date text, with an optional input format for legacy non-datetime input.
behaviors: `hour(t)` accepts datetime scalars and datetime arrays.
The output shape matches the input shape.
Hour values are returned in 24-hour clock form.
Documented legacy binary64 serial date numbers and date text return double hour values with matching shape.
Single-precision and all eight typed-integer legacy serial inputs are a gated RunMat extension; exact native values are range-checked before one binary64 serial-date conversion.

examples.description: Extract the hour from a scalar datetime
Extract hours from a datetime array

faqs.question: What clock convention does `hour` use?
faqs.answer: It returns 24-hour clock values such as `0`, `13`, or `23`.

faqs.question: Does `hour` preserve the input shape?
faqs.answer: Yes. The numeric output has the same size as the input datetime array.

faqs.question: Does `hour` run on the GPU?
faqs.answer: No. datetime values are host-side objects, so `hour` executes on the CPU.

gpu_residency: Documented `hour` forms are host-side. RunMat can admit resident legacy numeric input as an extension, gathers it non-destructively through the exact owner, and returns the documented host double result.
gpu_behavior: `hour` does not dispatch a GPU kernel. Explicit resident input is a separately gated RunMat extension, while internal automatic residency can gather transparently.
